SCOPE (PRINCIPAL-locked WHAT): the team-launcher + its activation must STRUCTURALLY guarantee three things:
1. CHAIN OF COMMAND AT LAUNCH. PRINCIPAL addresses ONLY POLYBIUS; POLYBIUS supervises PLINY (directs + verifies hand-backs via bw); PLINY spins up the CAPTAINs. Activation must make this explicit so PRINCIPAL is NEVER pointed at PLINY and the seats know their place -- NOT co-equal independent panes the PRINCIPAL coordinates separately.
2. GAUNTLET-BY-DEFAULT. The full gauntlet (DAEDALUS->ARGUS->ADA->VERA->CATO + NOMOS) is the DEFAULT, not a seat discretionary call. A seat must not be able to silently run solo with one checker.
3. VARIABLE TEAM COMPOSITION. The team is not always POLYBIUS+PLINY. Design-heavy arcs also include MAJOR_CHIRON (team-architect) + MAJOR_HAMILTON (workflow architect); the launcher must support launching + PLACING them in the chain, not assume the two-seat default.

MOTIVATING CASE (AR-7 / nws-iey, 2026-06-20): a POLYBIUS seat was activated with an INCOMPLETE instruction (no chain-of-command established, no team composition named), ran SOLO as its own orchestrator, spawned CAPTAINs directly, and self-certified verification depth (one CATO, no gauntlet). Recovery needed an independent CATO re-verify + a user-tier-driven merge. The launcher this arc builds must make that failure STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE. Treat AR-7 as the case study.

GAUNTLET: full DAEDALUS->ARGUS->ADA->VERA->CATO->NOMOS; substrate canon (team-launcher + gauntlet-setup skill + operating-disciplines + role files), so CATO/NOMOS carry extra weight. DESIGN-HEAVY -> bring in CHIRON + HAMILTON for the design phase (do not assume the two-seat default).

REGISTRY: reuse stoa--reg (ONE registry); coordinate the composition/manifest with the builder-deploy cookie-cutter follow-on (user-tier u--9s2) so the two do not diverge.

DOGFOOD: sign every comm with [from: <NAME> | sid <session-id>] from turn one.

ARC-68 LIVE FINDING (surfaced by user-tier Polybius_the_Stoa while DRIVING the launch, 2026-06-20) -- a CONCRETE launcher-correctness defect, gift-wrapped for this arc:

DEFECT: the launcher record-seat step SILENTLY FAILS on a pwsh-driven launch. record-seat.ps1 runs in pwsh and calls "& bw attach ..."; but bw is NOT on the PowerShell PATH on this machine (only the bash PATH). So the bw call fails command-resolution, is caught by record-seat.ps1's try/catch, and is mis-reported as the BENIGN warning "expected on a workspace without the registry ticket". The-stoa HAS stoa--reg -- the real cause is the PATH, not a missing ticket.

IMPACT: the seat registry (the Arc-67 / stoa--p7c deliverable) does NOT actually get written from a pwsh-driven launch -- a latent Arc-67 bug. The launch itself succeeds (claude IS on the pwsh PATH); only the best-effort record fails.

PROOF: the exact attach command record-seat runs (bw attach stoa--reg <temp> --name seat-registry.jsonl) SUCCEEDS when run from bash (exit 0, registry row written); the SAME command fails from pwsh because Get-Command bw returns nothing there.

BRIDGE (not a fix): I recorded the FM seat (POLYBIUS_the-stoa) to stoa--reg manually via bash, so the registry has the row. This is a temporary bridge, NOT the fix.

FOR THE ARC (DC-adjacent to the chain-of-command/gauntlet-default/composition work): make record-seat + the launcher invoke bw in a pwsh-resolvable way (resolve bw via the bash PATH or call it through bash) AND fail-LOUD with the REAL error rather than mis-attributing every failure to the benign no-ticket case. The mis-attribution is itself a correctness hazard -- it hid a total registry-write failure behind a "benign" label. This is live empirical brittleness, discovered by dogfooding the launch the arc is meant to harden.

[from: POLYBIUS_the-stoa | sid 67aa59a3-91e9-4c0c-acf0-c3aae3463b04 | the-stoa]

MIS-ATTRIBUTION CONFIRMED. record-seat.ps1 L119-128: the & bw attach call sits in a try; ANY failure (including a pwsh CommandNotFound) is caught at L122 and collapsed at L126 to the single benign message 'expected on a workspace without the registry ticket'. The catch never inspects the actual error, so a total registry-write failure is indistinguishable from the legitimate no-ticket case. This is the correctness hazard user-tier named: a fail-OPEN that hid a fail.

SCOPE READ (FM): this is owner-authorized into Arc 68 (user-tier, the arc owner, handed it FOR THE ARC) and is a TARGETED fix at the record-seat call site -- bw invocation + honest error-attribution -- NOT a registry/schema rebuild, so it stays clear of the 'do not rebuild the Arc-67 identity layer' out-of-scope line.
